subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram group: cross-agent sessions_list visibility mismatch causes one-way sessions_send failure

question: Should cross-agent `sessions_send` be authorized by A2A policy independently from `sessions_list`/`sessions_history`/`session_status` visibility for Telegram group multi-agent setups?
rationale: The code path is clear, but the fix changes a cross-agent authorization boundary and current docs/tests intentionally make cross-agent access require `tools.sessions.visibility="all"`.

options.title: Approve bounded send-only A2A
options.body: Allow `sessions_send` when A2A permits the requester-target pair, while keeping list/history/status visibility-gated and requiring focused tests plus live Telegram A/B proof.

options.title: Use per-capability visibility as canonical
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48785 as the product path and defer this issue until structured send/list/history/status visibility is designed.

options.title: Keep current fail-closed behavior
options.body: Require the reporter's compact A/B repro table before changing policy and continue treating shared Telegram group membership as insufficient by itself.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded send-only A2A
recommendation.body: Allow `sessions_send` when A2A permits the requester-target pair, while keeping list/history/status visibility-gated and requiring focused tests plus live Telegram A/B proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant session security scoping and helper-split history points to this owner as the best available reviewer for the authorization contract.
